answer_text:
Interpreting the question as: **how many consecutive zeros are immediately to the left of the final digit?**

Let

\[
N=2009^{2011}.
\]

The last digit is easy:

\[
2009 \equiv 9 \pmod{10},\qquad 9^{\text{odd}}\equiv 9 \pmod{10},
\]

so the last digit is \(9\).

Now check how many zeros come before it.

### 1. Check the last two digits

Since

\[
2009 \equiv 9 \pmod{100},
\]

we need \(9^{2011}\pmod{100}\). We have

\[
9^{10}\equiv 1 \pmod{100}.
\]

Because

\[
2011\equiv 1 \pmod{10},
\]

it follows that

\[
9^{2011}\equiv 9^1\equiv 9 \pmod{100}.
\]

So the last two digits are

\[
09.
\]

Thus at least one zero precedes the last digit.

### 2. Check whether there are two zeros

Now work modulo \(1000\). Since

\[
2009 \equiv 9 \pmod{1000},
\]

we need

\[
9^{2011}\pmod{1000}.
\]

Using Euler’s theorem, \(\varphi(1000)=400\), so

\[
9^{400}\equiv 1 \pmod{1000}.
\]

Since

\[
2011=5\cdot 400+11,
\]

we get

\[
9^{2011}\equiv 9^{11}\pmod{1000}.
\]

Compute:

\[
9^2=81,
\]

\[
9^4\equiv 81^2=6561\equiv 561 \pmod{1000},
\]

\[
9^5\equiv 561\cdot 9=5049\equiv 49 \pmod{1000},
\]

\[
9^{10}\equiv 49^2=2401\equiv 401 \pmod{1000},
\]

\[
9^{11}\equiv 401\cdot 9=3609\equiv 609 \pmod{1000}.
\]

Thus

\[
2009^{2011}\equiv 609 \pmod{1000}.
\]

So the last three digits are

\[
609.
\]

The digit immediately before the final \(9\) is \(0\), but the digit before that is \(6\), not \(0\). Therefore exactly one zero precedes the last digit.

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
